subject: Behavioral Economics
title: FOMO: Fear of Missing Out
description: A fast breakdown of FOMO: Fear of Missing Out for builders.

hook.text: Everyone is posting about a flash sale. You were not planning to buy anything. Twenty minutes later, your cart is full.

buildup.text: FOMO is the anxiety that others are getting benefits you're missing. Social media amplifies it by making others' gains.

discovery.text: Przybylski found FOMO is driven by unmet psychological needs: autonomy, competence, and relatedness.

twist.text: Marketers engineer FOMO deliberately. Live viewer counts, sold-out warnings, and social sharing buttons all trigger.

climax.text: When FOMO strikes, ask: would I buy this if nobody else knew about the deal?

punchline.text: FOMO isn't about missing out. It's about belonging.

quiz.question: What psychological needs drive FOMO according to Przybylski?

details.summary: FOMO is the anxiety that others are enjoying rewarding experiences you are missing. Marketers leverage this fear through limited-time offers, social media showcases of others' purchases, and exclusive access to drive impulsive buying decisions.
details.whyItMatters: FOMO is one of the strongest emotional drivers of consumer behavior in the social media age. It transforms rational purchasing decisions into emotionally urgent ones, bypassing careful evaluation of whether the product is actually needed.
takeaways: FOMO converts rational purchase decisions into emotional urgency
Social media amplifies FOMO by showcasing others' experiences constantly
Limited access and exclusivity are the primary FOMO triggers in marketing

faq.question: How does social media amplify FOMO in purchasing?
faq.answer: Social media creates a constant stream of others' purchases, experiences, and lifestyle displays. Each post creates a comparison point that generates regret about what you do not have and urgency to acquire similar social proof.

faq.question: How can consumers protect themselves from FOMO-driven purchases?
faq.answer: Implement a 24-hour waiting period for non-essential purchases. Recognize that curated social media creates unrealistic comparisons. Ask whether you would still want the item if nobody could see you bought it.
